digital_hardware_refresh_cycle.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program definition and a declared spatial, temporal, and methodological boundary.
digital_hardware_refresh_cycle.failure_behavior: Do not equate a procurement cycle with physical retirement, waste, or material loss.

electronics_solvents_leachate.unit: concentration and mass load by named compound, matrix, and reporting period
electronics_solvents_leachate.geography: named manufacturing, recycling, disposal, groundwater, or outfall site
electronics_solvents_leachate.transformation: Retain compound, process or waste source, release pathway, matrix, flow, detection limit, blank, treatment, receiving medium, and source-apportionment evidence.

electronics_solvents_leachate.failure_behavior: Do not infer leaching from solvent use or assign an electronics source from detection alone.

recreational_boating_fuel_leakage.unit: litres released, recovered, and remaining by incident and material
recreational_boating_fuel_leakage.geography: named vessel, marina or water body, incident, response, and affected shoreline
recreational_boating_fuel_leakage.transformation: Retain vessel and fuel, source, cause, quantity, water entry, containment, recovery, weather, exposure, and report status.
recreational_boating_fuel_leakage.uncertainty: Coverage, reporting thresholds, method changes, spatial boundaries, attribution, and incomplete records affect comparison.
recreational_boating_fuel_leakage.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program, method, permit, or investigation and retain its explicit boundary.
recreational_boating_fuel_leakage.failure_behavior: Do not infer a release from boating activity, sheen reports without confirmation, or fuel carried onboard.

solar_panel_refining_waste.unit: tonnes by material, process, hazardous classification, treatment, recovery, and destination
solar_panel_refining_waste.geography: named mineral, refining or manufacturing facility, supply-chain stage, and jurisdiction
solar_panel_refining_waste.transformation: Retain product and process boundary, input purity, reagents, waste stream, composition, mass balance, recovery, treatment, disposal, and uncertainty.
solar_panel_refining_waste.uncertainty: Coverage, reporting thresholds, method changes, spatial boundaries, attribution, and incomplete records affect comparison.
solar_panel_refining_waste.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program, method, permit, or investigation and retain its explicit boundary.
solar_panel_refining_waste.failure_behavior: Do not assign all mineral refining waste to solar products or infer exposure from generation alone.

supertanker_sound_waves.unit: source level, received level, frequency spectrum, duration, range, and vessel state
supertanker_sound_waves.geography: named vessel class, route, speed, ocean conditions, receiver, and monitoring period
supertanker_sound_waves.transformation: Retain vessel, speed, draft, propeller and machinery state, sound metric and frequency, propagation, background, receiver, and uncertainty.
supertanker_sound_waves.uncertainty: Coverage, reporting thresholds, method changes, spatial boundaries, attribution, and incomplete records affect comparison.
supertanker_sound_waves.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program, method, permit, or investigation and retain its explicit boundary.
supertanker_sound_waves.failure_behavior: Do not infer biological harm from vessel class or source level without received exposure and response.

tar_sands_tailings_ponds.unit: cubic metres, hectares, water and solids composition, seepage, reclamation, and incident status separately
tar_sands_tailings_ponds.geography: named mine, tailings facility, monitoring network, watershed, and reporting year
tar_sands_tailings_ponds.transformation: Retain facility and process, fluid and solids volume, chemistry, dam and liner condition, seepage, water balance, treatment, reclamation, incidents, and uncertainty.
tar_sands_tailings_ponds.uncertainty: Coverage, reporting thresholds, method changes, spatial boundaries, attribution, and incomplete records affect comparison.
tar_sands_tailings_ponds.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program, method, permit, or investigation and retain its explicit boundary.
tar_sands_tailings_ponds.failure_behavior: Do not infer release, toxicity, or reclamation failure from pond area alone.

tidal_turbine_marine_hazard.unit: device hours, rotor speed, collision or encounter observations, sound, habitat area, and response separately
tidal_turbine_marine_hazard.geography: named project, device, tidal channel, receptor species, and monitoring design
tidal_turbine_marine_hazard.transformation: Retain device and operation, flow, species, detection, encounter and collision evidence, sound, habitat, controls, baseline, and uncertainty.
tidal_turbine_marine_hazard.uncertainty: Coverage, reporting thresholds, method changes, spatial boundaries, attribution, and incomplete records affect comparison.
tidal_turbine_marine_hazard.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program, method, permit, or investigation and retain its explicit boundary.
tidal_turbine_marine_hazard.failure_behavior: Do not infer mortality or population harm from device presence or modeled encounter alone.

wind_farm_ecosystem_siting.unit: hectares, turbine count, distance, modeled collision exposure, and habitat overlap by receptor
wind_farm_ecosystem_siting.geography: named project, alternative, construction footprint, habitat, species, and permit boundary
wind_farm_ecosystem_siting.transformation: Retain alternative sites, footprint, roads and lines, habitat, migration, species surveys, avoidance, curtailment, mitigation, permit, and monitoring.
wind_farm_ecosystem_siting.uncertainty: Coverage, reporting thresholds, method changes, spatial boundaries, attribution, and incomplete records affect comparison.
wind_farm_ecosystem_siting.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program, method, permit, or investigation and retain its explicit boundary.
wind_farm_ecosystem_siting.failure_behavior: Do not infer ecosystem harm from project capacity, lease area, or overlap alone.

seed_germination_drops.unit: percent germination, emergence, time to emergence, and seedling survival by crop, variety, and treatment
seed_germination_drops.geography: named crop or wild taxon, seed lot, soil or growth medium, climate treatment, and study period
seed_germination_drops.transformation: Retain species and variety, seed lot and viability, dormancy treatment, temperature, moisture, salinity, pathogens, soil, replication, emergence, and survival.
seed_germination_drops.uncertainty: Coverage, reporting thresholds, method changes, spatial boundaries, attribution, and incomplete records affect comparison.
seed_germination_drops.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program, method, permit, or investigation and retain its explicit boundary.
seed_germination_drops.failure_behavior: Do not infer field yield or a climate trend from one seed lot or laboratory treatment.

suburban_slum_expansion_areas.unit: hectares, households, people, tenure status, and service access reported separately
suburban_slum_expansion_areas.geography: named settlement, city, administrative boundary, and observation year
suburban_slum_expansion_areas.transformation: Retain mapped boundary, imagery or enumeration method, housing and tenure definition, population, water, sanitation, drainage, roads, electricity, hazards, and uncertainty.
suburban_slum_expansion_areas.uncertainty: Sampling coverage, method, boundary, attribution, natural variability, and incomplete reporting affect comparisons.
suburban_slum_expansion_areas.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program and a fixed taxonomic, geographic, temporal, and methodological boundary.
suburban_slum_expansion_areas.failure_behavior: Do not use slum as an unbounded label or infer deprivation, illegality, migration cause, or expansion from one image.

coastal_overfishing_scars.unit: biomass, fishing mortality, catch, size structure, habitat condition, and recovery status by assessed stock
coastal_overfishing_scars.geography: named coastal stock, fishery, management area, habitat, and assessment year
coastal_overfishing_scars.transformation: Retain stock, gear, effort, catch, biomass and mortality reference points, habitat disturbance, bycatch, management, recovery period, and uncertainty.
coastal_overfishing_scars.uncertainty: Sampling coverage, method, boundary, attribution, natural variability, and incomplete reporting affect comparisons.
coastal_overfishing_scars.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program and a fixed taxonomic, geographic, temporal, and methodological boundary.
coastal_overfishing_scars.failure_behavior: Do not call a low catch, altered habitat, or one depleted stock a persistent coastal scar without stock and habitat evidence.

hydro_hegemony_river_tensions.unit: flow, allocation, withdrawals, treaty-compliance indicators, cooperative events, and dispute events separately
hydro_hegemony_river_tensions.geography: named basin, riparian jurisdictions, agreement, allocation period, and event
hydro_hegemony_river_tensions.transformation: Retain hydrology, demand, allocation rule, infrastructure operation, treaty, compliance, negotiation, cooperation, dispute actor, event source, and uncertainty.
hydro_hegemony_river_tensions.uncertainty: Sampling coverage, method, boundary, attribution, natural variability, and incomplete reporting affect comparisons.
hydro_hegemony_river_tensions.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program and a fixed taxonomic, geographic, temporal, and methodological boundary.
hydro_hegemony_river_tensions.failure_behavior: Do not infer conflict from scarcity, upstream position, infrastructure, or political rhetoric alone.

marine_biodeposits_loss.metric_name: Bivalve biodeposition flux and benthic response
marine_biodeposits_loss.unit: grams carbon, nitrogen, or solids per square metre and time with benthic oxygen and community response separately
marine_biodeposits_loss.geography: named farm or reef, species, stocking density, current regime, seabed station, and season
marine_biodeposits_loss.transformation: Retain species, biomass, feeding and feces method, current, depth, sediment, background deposition, oxygen, benthic community, harvest, and uncertainty.
marine_biodeposits_loss.uncertainty: Sampling coverage, method, boundary, attribution, natural variability, and incomplete reporting affect comparisons.
marine_biodeposits_loss.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program and a fixed taxonomic, geographic, temporal, and methodological boundary.
marine_biodeposits_loss.failure_behavior: Do not infer ecosystem loss from lower deposition or aquaculture change without a defined baseline and benthic response.

marine_biome_displacement.unit: kilometres, square kilometres, species composition, thermal-displacement index, and depth shift separately
marine_biome_displacement.geography: named marine region, taxonomic community, temperature field, baseline, depth range, and period
marine_biome_displacement.transformation: Retain taxon and survey, temperature and depth, baseline, currents, habitat, fishing, sampling effort, range edge, colonization and loss, and uncertainty.
marine_biome_displacement.uncertainty: Sampling coverage, method, boundary, attribution, natural variability, and incomplete reporting affect comparisons.
marine_biome_displacement.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program and a fixed taxonomic, geographic, temporal, and methodological boundary.
marine_biome_displacement.failure_behavior: Do not call a temperature anomaly biome displacement without observed community redistribution and comparable sampling.

marine_mammal_migration_drifts.metric_name: Marine-mammal migration timing and route shift
marine_mammal_migration_drifts.unit: days, kilometres, occupancy, passage rate, and route probability by species and population
marine_mammal_migration_drifts.geography: named population, migration corridor, observation platform, season, and baseline
marine_mammal_migration_drifts.transformation: Retain species and population, tag or survey method, observation effort, timing, route, prey, temperature, ice, noise, vessel traffic, breeding state, and uncertainty.
marine_mammal_migration_drifts.uncertainty: Sampling coverage, method, boundary, attribution, natural variability, and incomplete reporting affect comparisons.
marine_mammal_migration_drifts.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program and a fixed taxonomic, geographic, temporal, and methodological boundary.
marine_mammal_migration_drifts.failure_behavior: Do not infer migration change from sightings alone or attribute it to climate without prey, habitat, effort, and alternate-driver analysis.

understory_moisture_losses.unit: volumetric soil water, fuel moisture, humidity, and anomaly from a fixed baseline reported separately
understory_moisture_losses.geography: named forest plot, depth, understory layer, vegetation type, season, and sensor network
understory_moisture_losses.transformation: Retain soil depth and method, humidity, fuel moisture, canopy, precipitation, evapotranspiration, temperature, groundwater, disturbance, and uncertainty.
understory_moisture_losses.uncertainty: Sampling coverage, method, boundary, attribution, natural variability, and incomplete reporting affect comparisons.
understory_moisture_losses.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program and a fixed taxonomic, geographic, temporal, and methodological boundary.
understory_moisture_losses.failure_behavior: Do not infer ecosystem damage or persistent drying from one sensor, layer, or season.

sub_polar_soil_instability.metric_name: Subpolar ground deformation and thaw condition
sub_polar_soil_instability.unit: centimetres displacement, active-layer thickness, ground temperature, subsidence, and failure area separately
sub_polar_soil_instability.geography: named subpolar site, landform, permafrost zone, infrastructure or ecosystem, and monitoring period
sub_polar_soil_instability.transformation: Retain ground ice, temperature, active layer, soil and drainage, snow, vegetation, slope, disturbance, deformation method, baseline, and uncertainty.
sub_polar_soil_instability.uncertainty: Sampling coverage, method, boundary, attribution, natural variability, and incomplete reporting affect comparisons.
sub_polar_soil_instability.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program and a fixed taxonomic, geographic, temporal, and methodological boundary.
sub_polar_soil_instability.failure_behavior: Do not infer permafrost-driven instability from latitude, air temperature, or one deformation observation.

seaweed_aquaculture_stresses.unit: tonnes, growth rate, mortality, disease prevalence, nutrient condition, and crop loss by species and farm
seaweed_aquaculture_stresses.geography: named farm, cultivated species and strain, water body, production cycle, and monitoring design
seaweed_aquaculture_stresses.transformation: Retain species and strain, seed source, density, gear, temperature, nutrients, light, disease, epiphytes, storms, grazers, chemicals, harvest, and uncertainty.
seaweed_aquaculture_stresses.uncertainty: Sampling coverage, method, boundary, attribution, natural variability, and incomplete reporting affect comparisons.
seaweed_aquaculture_stresses.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative program and a fixed taxonomic, geographic, temporal, and methodological boundary.
seaweed_aquaculture_stresses.failure_behavior: Do not generalize one farm outcome to wild seaweed or infer cause from production loss alone.

fossil_fuel_pipeline_protests.unit: event count, participants where reported, actors, event type, fatalities, and geographic coordinates reported separately
fossil_fuel_pipeline_protests.geography: named event site, administrative area, country, reporting period, and source set
fossil_fuel_pipeline_protests.cadence: event, seasonal, or annual update with a fixed review boundary
fossil_fuel_pipeline_protests.transformation: Retain event date, location, actors, event type, issue coding, source count, source quality, participant estimate, fatalities, notes, coverage period, and coding uncertainty.
fossil_fuel_pipeline_protests.uncertainty: Coverage, detection, reporting, method, boundary, attribution, and natural variability affect comparison and interpretation.
fossil_fuel_pipeline_protests.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative method and a declared geographic, temporal, biological, or event boundary; no universal threshold is implied.
fossil_fuel_pipeline_protests.failure_behavior: Do not infer a causal environmental condition, public consensus, project impact, or protest trend from an isolated event, media volume, or a pipeline mention alone.

genetically_modified_pollen_drift.unit: pollen concentration, outcrossing frequency, hybrid occurrence, or trait detection by taxon, distance, and sampling method
genetically_modified_pollen_drift.geography: named crop, engineered event, receptor population, field layout, sampling transect, flowering window, and season
genetically_modified_pollen_drift.cadence: event, seasonal, or annual update with a fixed review boundary
genetically_modified_pollen_drift.transformation: Retain donor and receptor taxa, engineered event, compatibility, flowering overlap, distance, wind and pollinator context, seed movement, volunteer plants, assay, detection limit, and uncertainty.
genetically_modified_pollen_drift.uncertainty: Coverage, detection, reporting, method, boundary, attribution, and natural variability affect comparison and interpretation.
genetically_modified_pollen_drift.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative method and a declared geographic, temporal, biological, or event boundary; no universal threshold is implied.
genetically_modified_pollen_drift.failure_behavior: Do not infer ecological harm, persistent introgression, or pollinator decline from pollen movement or a single trait detection without compatible reproduction, persistence, exposure, and effect evidence.

macrofungal_mycelium_decay.unit: fungal biomass, hyphal length, community composition, litter-mass loss, respiration, or nutrient-mineralization rate with method stated
macrofungal_mycelium_decay.geography: named soil plot, forest type, horizon, substrate, treatment, season, and sampling design
macrofungal_mycelium_decay.cadence: event, seasonal, or annual update with a fixed review boundary
macrofungal_mycelium_decay.transformation: Retain fungal guild, taxonomic method, soil depth, substrate, moisture, temperature, disturbance, land-use history, decomposition protocol, nutrient flux, replication, and uncertainty.
macrofungal_mycelium_decay.uncertainty: Coverage, detection, reporting, method, boundary, attribution, and natural variability affect comparison and interpretation.
macrofungal_mycelium_decay.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative method and a declared geographic, temporal, biological, or event boundary; no universal threshold is implied.
macrofungal_mycelium_decay.failure_behavior: Do not call lower fruiting-body counts or one decomposition measurement mycelial decay, and do not attribute a change without comparable soil, substrate, climate, and disturbance observations.

invasive_seaweed_blooms.unit: occupied hectares, percent cover, biomass, patch density, or new verified occurrences by named taxon and method
invasive_seaweed_blooms.geography: named taxon, coastline, lagoon, estuary, habitat, depth range, survey footprint, and observation period
invasive_seaweed_blooms.cadence: event, seasonal, or annual update with a fixed review boundary
invasive_seaweed_blooms.transformation: Retain taxon verification, native status, introduction history, survey effort, occupied area, cover or biomass, fragmentation and vector context, habitat overlap, eradication status, and uncertainty.
invasive_seaweed_blooms.uncertainty: Coverage, detection, reporting, method, boundary, attribution, and natural variability affect comparison and interpretation.
invasive_seaweed_blooms.threshold_provenance: Use the named authoritative method and a declared geographic, temporal, biological, or event boundary; no universal threshold is implied.
invasive_seaweed_blooms.failure_behavior: Do not call native seasonal seaweed growth an invasion, combine taxa, infer a bloom from one occurrence, or infer impact without comparable native-community and habitat observations.

peatland_degradations.unit: hectares by condition class, drainage status, land use, and assessment year
peatland_degradations.geography: mapped peatland complex, basin, country, or reporting region
peatland_degradations.transformation: Retain peatland boundary, condition class, drainage status, land use, fire history, mapping method, and uncertainty; compare like classifications over time.
peatland_degradations.uncertainty: Peat depth, drainage mapping, land-cover classification, cloud cover, restoration status, and inconsistent national inventories affect estimates.
peatland_degradations.threshold_provenance: Use the named assessment method and regional condition classes; no universal degraded-area threshold is implied.
peatland_degradations.failure_behavior: Do not infer degradation from fire, emissions, or land-cover change alone when peatland extent and condition are unverified.

wetland_peat_fires.metric_name: Peat-fire burned area and carbon emission
wetland_peat_fires.unit: hectares burned and tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent with peat depth, combustion factor, and reporting interval stated
wetland_peat_fires.geography: mapped peatland fire perimeter, province, basin, or country
wetland_peat_fires.cadence: event-based with seasonal and annual summaries
wetland_peat_fires.transformation: Intersect quality-controlled fire detections or perimeters with verified peatland extent; retain burn depth, persistence, fuel moisture, emission factors, and cloud or smoke limitations.
wetland_peat_fires.uncertainty: Subsurface smouldering, burn depth, peat bulk density, emission factors, obscured satellite detections, and repeated burning drive large uncertainty.
wetland_peat_fires.threshold_provenance: Use event-specific burned-area and emissions methods; fire detection is not equivalent to complete combustion accounting.
wetland_peat_fires.failure_behavior: Do not classify a wetland fire as a peat fire without spatial peatland confirmation, and never impute missing burned area as zero.

cooling_equity_gaps.metric_name: Heat exposure without safe and affordable cooling access
cooling_equity_gaps.unit: people or households, percentage, and cooling-energy affordability burden within a stated heat threshold and service definition
cooling_equity_gaps.geography: city, settlement, utility territory, country, or named vulnerable population
cooling_equity_gaps.transformation: Join heat exposure with housing, electricity access, service reliability, cooling-device access, affordability, and vulnerability data without treating equipment ownership alone as effective cooling.
cooling_equity_gaps.uncertainty: Informal housing, unreliable service, indoor conditions, device efficiency, energy prices, income, and population mobility limit comparability.
cooling_equity_gaps.threshold_provenance: Heat, affordability, and safe-cooling thresholds must come from the named local or assessment protocol.
cooling_equity_gaps.failure_behavior: Do not infer equitable cooling from national electrification or air-conditioner sales; mark missing household and service-quality coverage explicitly.

coral_larval_mortality.metric_name: Coral larval survival, settlement, and recruitment
coral_larval_mortality.unit: survival percentage, settlement percentage, or recruits per square meter by species and cohort
coral_larval_mortality.geography: named reef, nursery, settlement array, or experimental population
coral_larval_mortality.cadence: spawning-event and cohort based with annual synthesis
coral_larval_mortality.transformation: Retain species, life stage, parent condition, temperature, carbonate chemistry, settlement substrate, observation duration, method, and cohort denominator.
coral_larval_mortality.uncertainty: Spawning variability, dispersal, predation, settlement substrate, parental effects, heat, chemistry, disease, and sampling timing affect survival and recruitment.
coral_larval_mortality.threshold_provenance: Use species-, cohort-, and study-specific controls or reef baselines; no universal mortality threshold is implied.
coral_larval_mortality.failure_behavior: Do not infer larval mortality from adult bleaching, low coral cover, or absent recruits without life-stage-resolved observations.

tropospheric_ozone.unit: parts per billion using stated averaging time, instrument, quality status, and exposure window
tropospheric_ozone.geography: named regulatory monitor, airshed, urban area, agricultural region, or gridded model domain
tropospheric_ozone.cadence: hourly observations with daily and seasonal summaries
tropospheric_ozone.transformation: Retain monitor method, QA status, averaging time, meteorology, precursor regime, spatial coverage, and whether values are observed or modeled; compute exposure indices only from the named protocol.
tropospheric_ozone.uncertainty: Monitor siting, vertical mixing, transport, clouds, temperature, precursor chemistry, missing hours, and model resolution affect exposure estimates.
tropospheric_ozone.threshold_provenance: Use the applicable regulatory or ecological exposure standard and averaging period; no universal concentration threshold is substituted.
tropospheric_ozone.failure_behavior: Do not infer concentration from precursor emissions or temperature alone, and never mix stratospheric and ground-level observations.

coral_reef_fragmentation.unit: fragment count, percent damaged framework, rugosity, or three-dimensional complexity by mapped reef area and survey date
coral_reef_fragmentation.geography: named reef tract, incident perimeter, survey transect, or restoration site
coral_reef_fragmentation.transformation: Retain damage mechanism, reef zone, species or growth form, baseline structure, survey resolution, fragment size, live tissue, and recovery or stabilization status.
coral_reef_fragmentation.uncertainty: Pre-event baselines, survey visibility, storm attribution, overlapping chronic stress, three-dimensional reconstruction, and detection of buried fragments affect estimates.
coral_reef_fragmentation.threshold_provenance: Use incident-specific or monitoring-program damage classes; fragmentation is not inferred from coral cover alone.
coral_reef_fragmentation.failure_behavior: Do not classify bleaching, mortality, or low cover as physical fragmentation without observed breakage, dislodgement, or framework discontinuity.

glacial_siltation_streams.metric_name: Glacier-fed stream suspended-sediment concentration and flux
glacial_siltation_streams.unit: milligrams per liter and tonnes per day or season with discharge, grain-size, and sampling method stated
glacial_siltation_streams.geography: named proglacial stream, gauging station, downstream lake, reservoir, or fjord
glacial_siltation_streams.cadence: sub-daily during events and melt season with annual sediment-load synthesis
glacial_siltation_streams.transformation: Pair concentration or turbidity calibration with discharge; retain glacier cover, melt contribution, event type, sampling verticals, grain size, bedload exclusions, rating-curve uncertainty, and deposition boundary.
glacial_siltation_streams.uncertainty: Short-lived peaks, sparse winter data, rating-curve hysteresis, bedload, changing glacier drainage, grain size, and station placement affect annual loads.
glacial_siltation_streams.threshold_provenance: Use station- and basin-specific concentration-discharge relations and habitat or infrastructure criteria; no universal siltation threshold is implied.
glacial_siltation_streams.failure_behavior: Do not infer sediment flux from meltwater volume, turbidity, or glacier retreat alone, and do not transfer a rating curve between basins without validation.

blue_carbon_habitat_loss.metric_name: Coastal blue-carbon habitat area and carbon-stock loss
blue_carbon_habitat_loss.unit: hectares lost and tonnes carbon or carbon dioxide equivalent released or sequestration capacity lost
blue_carbon_habitat_loss.geography: global assessment or named salt-marsh, mangrove, or seagrass assessment area
blue_carbon_habitat_loss.cadence: major global assessment or annual to multi-year inventory
blue_carbon_habitat_loss.transformation: Retain habitat class, mapped area, soil depth, carbon-stock method, disturbance type, baseline year, and whether release or avoided sequestration is estimated.
blue_carbon_habitat_loss.uncertainty: Below-ground stocks, erosion fate, remineralization, mapping resolution, and counterfactual sequestration vary by habitat and method.
blue_carbon_habitat_loss.threshold_provenance: Habitat-specific inventory method or IPCC wetlands accounting boundary.
blue_carbon_habitat_loss.failure_behavior: Do not convert habitat area directly to emissions without habitat-specific stock and disturbance factors.

glacier_calving_events.unit: meters of front-position change and cubic kilometers or gigatonnes of ice discharge per period
glacier_calving_events.geography: named marine-terminating glacier or ice shelf
glacier_calving_events.cadence: event-based with seasonal and annual synthesis
glacier_calving_events.transformation: Retain glacier geometry, front position, velocity, thickness, grounding line, observation sensor, event boundary, and uncertainty; separate normal calving from sustained retreat or disintegration.
glacier_calving_events.uncertainty: Cloud cover, mélange, front delineation, thickness, density, and poorly observed submarine geometry affect event and flux estimates.
glacier_calving_events.threshold_provenance: Glacier-specific observation record and mass-budget method.
glacier_calving_events.failure_behavior: Do not classify a single iceberg release as climate-driven retreat without a longer front-position and mass-budget record.

volatile_organic_compounds.unit: parts per billion by compound with sampling duration, method, and photochemical reactivity
volatile_organic_compounds.geography: named monitor, facility boundary, community, or airshed
volatile_organic_compounds.cadence: hourly, integrated canister sample, or campaign-specific
volatile_organic_compounds.transformation: Retain compound identity, detection limit, sampling duration, method, QA status, source context, and reactivity; never sum compounds without an explicit mass or reactivity basis.
volatile_organic_compounds.uncertainty: Species volatility, sampling losses, detection limits, spatial gradients, and rapidly changing chemistry affect measurements.
volatile_organic_compounds.threshold_provenance: Compound-specific EPA method and applicable air-toxic or ozone-precursor assessment.
volatile_organic_compounds.failure_behavior: Do not treat total hydrocarbons, odor, or an unspecified organic-gas signal as a validated compound concentration.

nighttime_heat_retention.unit: degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit with urban and reference sites, height, local time, and averaging window stated
nighttime_heat_retention.geography: named city and matched rural or intra-urban reference network
nighttime_heat_retention.cadence: hourly observations with nightly, seasonal, and heat-event summaries
nighttime_heat_retention.transformation: Pair comparable canopy-layer air-temperature observations; retain station siting, height, land cover, local time, weather, season, and reference definition. Surface temperature remains separate.
nighttime_heat_retention.uncertainty: Station siting, urban morphology, wind, cloud cover, humidity, advection, season, and the rural reference affect the measured difference.
nighttime_heat_retention.threshold_provenance: City-specific paired observations and EPA heat-island measurement guidance; no universal nighttime threshold is implied.
nighttime_heat_retention.failure_behavior: Do not mix satellite surface temperature with near-surface air temperature or infer a citywide value from one unpaired station.

transformer_heat_failure_risk.unit: winding hot-spot temperature in degrees Celsius with percent rated load, ambient temperature, asset age, and insulation condition
transformer_heat_failure_risk.geography: named distribution or power transformer and its served circuit or substation
transformer_heat_failure_risk.cadence: continuous or sub-hourly condition monitoring with event and annual asset-health summaries
transformer_heat_failure_risk.transformation: Retain asset rating, load, ambient temperature, winding or oil temperature, cooling state, asset age, insulation condition, alarm threshold, and outage record; calculate thermal aging only with a documented equipment model.
transformer_heat_failure_risk.uncertainty: Sensor placement, unobserved winding hot spots, cooling performance, moisture, prior insulation damage, load harmonics, and asset-specific design affect inferred risk.
transformer_heat_failure_risk.threshold_provenance: Manufacturer limit, utility asset-health rule, or applicable IEEE thermal-loading method for the named transformer class.
transformer_heat_failure_risk.failure_behavior: Do not infer failure from regional heat or system load alone; require asset-level loading, temperature, condition, or a documented outage.

shelf_sea_hypoxia.unit: milligrams per liter or milliliters per liter dissolved oxygen with hypoxic area, water-column thickness, duration, depth, threshold and global site inventory reported separately
shelf_sea_hypoxia.geography: named continental-shelf survey grid, transect, bottom-water station network, model domain, or declared global assessment boundary
shelf_sea_hypoxia.cadence: continuous station observations or repeated seasonal surveys with annual synthesis and global assessment reviews
shelf_sea_hypoxia.transformation: Retain depth, distance above seabed, instrument and calibration, temperature, salinity, density structure, threshold, survey coverage, interpolation method, and whether the record is observed or modeled.
shelf_sea_hypoxia.uncertainty: Sparse transects, sensor drift, short-lived mixing, tidal and upwelling variability, threshold choice, and interpolation across unobserved shelf water affect area and duration estimates.
shelf_sea_hypoxia.threshold_provenance: Use the named monitoring program threshold, such as 2 milligrams per liter or 1.4 milliliters per liter, without treating thresholds from different programs as interchangeable.
shelf_sea_hypoxia.failure_behavior: Do not infer shelf-wide hypoxia from one low-oxygen station, substitute a global oxygen trend for local observations, or merge measurements that use incompatible depth and threshold definitions.

cloud_albedo_shift.unit: watts per square meter for shortwave, longwave, and net cloud radiative effect, reported separately with clear-sky definition and uncertainty
cloud_albedo_shift.geography: CERES footprint, declared grid, cloud regime, ocean basin, or global aggregation
cloud_albedo_shift.cadence: monthly observations with seasonal and annual anomaly review
cloud_albedo_shift.transformation: Compute cloudy-minus-clear or the declared CERES convention consistently; retain top-of-atmosphere versus surface boundary, shortwave, longwave, net flux, cloud height, optical depth, cloud fraction, instrument edition, sampling, and baseline.
cloud_albedo_shift.uncertainty: Clear-sky sampling, scene classification, cloud masking, diurnal sampling, instrument calibration, aerosol above clouds, surface albedo, and changing cloud regimes affect estimated trends.
cloud_albedo_shift.threshold_provenance: Use the named CERES product and a fixed sign convention; a present-day cooling effect does not determine the sign of a future feedback.
cloud_albedo_shift.failure_behavior: Do not report an unsigned albedo shift as warming or cooling, mix shortwave and net effects, or infer feedback from a single cloud property without radiative flux observations.

ozone_formation_pressure.unit: parts per billion ozone with compound-resolved volatile-organic precursors, nitrogen oxides, temperature, solar radiation, wind, and boundary-layer height reported separately
ozone_formation_pressure.geography: named regulatory monitor, urban airshed, freight corridor, or downwind receptor region
ozone_formation_pressure.cadence: hourly observations with episode-day and ozone-season summaries
ozone_formation_pressure.transformation: Time-align ozone, precursor, temperature, sunlight, wind, and mixing observations; retain monitor siting, fleet and emissions context, chemical regime, QA flags, and transported-background estimates.
ozone_formation_pressure.uncertainty: Nonlinear precursor chemistry, emissions inventories, transported ozone, monitor coverage, biogenic emissions, clouds, stagnation, and boundary-layer mixing affect attribution.
ozone_formation_pressure.threshold_provenance: Use the applicable regulatory ozone averaging period and an airshed-specific photochemical assessment; no universal precursor-response ratio is implied.
ozone_formation_pressure.failure_behavior: Do not attribute an ozone episode to heat, freight, or one precursor alone without time-aligned chemistry and meteorology.

estuary_eutrophication.unit: nitrogen and phosphorus concentration or load, chlorophyll-a, water clarity, dissolved oxygen, affected-system count and hypoxic area or duration reported separately
estuary_eutrophication.geography: named estuary, tributary, station network, assessment segment, or worldwide UNEP inventory boundary
estuary_eutrophication.cadence: event and seasonal sampling with annual, multi-year or global condition assessment
estuary_eutrophication.transformation: Retain nutrient species, concentration versus load, discharge, chlorophyll, clarity, oxygen depth, threshold, sampling coverage, residence time, salinity, treatment status, and observed versus modeled provenance.
estuary_eutrophication.uncertainty: Sparse sampling, tidal stage, river discharge, nutrient form, internal loading, residence time, stratification, algal composition, sensor drift, and threshold choice affect attribution and area estimates.
estuary_eutrophication.threshold_provenance: Use estuary-specific nutrient criteria or the named monitoring-program threshold; nitrogen, phosphorus, chlorophyll, clarity, and oxygen thresholds are not interchangeable.
estuary_eutrophication.failure_behavior: Do not infer a system-wide condition from one nutrient sample or treat a bloom, low-oxygen reading, or runoff event as sufficient without receiving-water evidence.

kelp_forest_collapse.unit: hectares and percent change relative to a fixed seasonal baseline
kelp_forest_collapse.geography: named kelp forest, coastline segment, sanctuary, or ecoregion
kelp_forest_collapse.cadence: seasonal observation with annual trend review
kelp_forest_collapse.transformation: Retain species, sensor or survey method, tidal and seasonal window, cloud and water-quality screening, mapped area, and baseline period.
kelp_forest_collapse.uncertainty: Canopy visibility, species life history, storms, seasonality, water clarity, and survey coverage can mimic or obscure ecological loss.
kelp_forest_collapse.threshold_provenance: Use the named monitoring programme and locally defined baseline; no universal collapse threshold is implied.
kelp_forest_collapse.failure_behavior: Do not infer loss from a single obscured image or compare unmatched seasons, sensors, or coastline boundaries.

aquifer_recharge_failure.unit: millimetres per year or cubic metres per year with aquifer and method stated
aquifer_recharge_failure.geography: named aquifer, recharge zone, catchment, or groundwater model domain
aquifer_recharge_failure.transformation: Retain precipitation and snowmelt input, evapotranspiration, land cover, soil and aquifer properties, stream leakage, pumping, model method, calibration period, and uncertainty.
aquifer_recharge_failure.uncertainty: Recharge is commonly modelled rather than directly observed and varies strongly with geology, antecedent moisture, land cover, and climate.
aquifer_recharge_failure.threshold_provenance: Compare like-for-like estimates against a named aquifer baseline and water-balance method.
aquifer_recharge_failure.failure_behavior: Do not infer recharge decline from groundwater-level decline alone because pumping and discharge can lower levels without changing recharge.

old_growth_forest_logging.unit: hectares harvested by method and reporting period
old_growth_forest_logging.geography: named forest management unit using an explicit old-growth definition
old_growth_forest_logging.transformation: Retain the operational old-growth definition, harvest type and intensity, road footprint, pre-harvest carbon and structure, product fate, regeneration plan, and mapping uncertainty.
old_growth_forest_logging.uncertainty: Old-growth definitions vary by forest type and jurisdiction, while selective harvest and collateral damage can be underdetected remotely.
old_growth_forest_logging.threshold_provenance: Use the named inventory definition and management boundary; do not apply a universal age threshold.
old_growth_forest_logging.failure_behavior: Do not label all mature-forest management as old-growth logging or infer net emissions without ecosystem and harvested-product carbon accounting.

rainforest_savannization.unit: hectares and percent of fixed forest baseline reclassified with persistence threshold
rainforest_savannization.geography: named tropical-forest biome, ecoregion, or fixed analysis grid
rainforest_savannization.cadence: annual land-cover update with multi-year persistence review
rainforest_savannization.transformation: Retain forest definition, canopy and vegetation-class thresholds, sensor, fire and harvest history, baseline, minimum persistence duration, rainfall and aridity context, and classification uncertainty.
rainforest_savannization.uncertainty: Temporary canopy loss, fire scars, plantations, seasonal phenology, sensor change, and gradual degradation can be confused with a persistent biome transition.
rainforest_savannization.threshold_provenance: Require a named regional ecological classification and persistent forest-to-open-vegetation transition; do not infer a tipping point from tree-cover loss alone.
rainforest_savannization.failure_behavior: Do not publish a transition when only disturbance, degradation, or temporary canopy loss is observed without persistent vegetation-state change.

pollen_allergen_spikes.unit: grains per cubic metre by taxon and sampling interval, with season start, end, duration, and cumulative count reported separately
pollen_allergen_spikes.geography: named pollen-monitoring station and its stated representativeness area
pollen_allergen_spikes.cadence: daily during the taxon-specific pollen season with annual season summaries
pollen_allergen_spikes.transformation: Retain taxon, sampler, counting protocol, station, start and end definition, cumulative count, frost date, temperature, rainfall, wind, land cover, missing days, quality flags, and uncertainty.
pollen_allergen_spikes.uncertainty: Different samplers are not always comparable for absolute counts; station coverage, taxon identification, wind transport, rainfall washout, local vegetation, missing observations, and season definitions affect results.
pollen_allergen_spikes.threshold_provenance: Use the monitoring network method and taxon-specific clinical or public-health context; spike is not a universal concentration threshold.
pollen_allergen_spikes.failure_behavior: Do not compare unmatched sampler methods, infer a local plant source from an airborne count, or equate season length with exposure intensity.

fisheries_range_redistribution.metric_name: Marine-stock distribution centroid and boundary change
fisheries_range_redistribution.unit: kilometres and degrees latitude or metres depth per decade, with occupancy, biomass weighting, survey domain, and uncertainty stated
fisheries_range_redistribution.geography: named stock, species, survey programme, shelf, management area, or transboundary marine region
fisheries_range_redistribution.cadence: annual fisheries-independent survey with multi-year trend review
fisheries_range_redistribution.transformation: Retain taxon and stock, survey gear, effort, season, depth, domain, detectability, biomass or occupancy weighting, centroid and boundary method, temperature and oxygen covariates, management boundaries, missing years, and uncertainty.
fisheries_range_redistribution.uncertainty: Survey coverage, gear catchability, seasonal movement, age structure, stock definition, population abundance, habitat, prey, fishing pressure, ocean variability, and model choice affect apparent shifts.
fisheries_range_redistribution.threshold_provenance: Use the named survey and DisMAP-compatible method; a changed catch location is not by itself a population-range shift.
fisheries_range_redistribution.failure_behavior: Do not infer climate causation from landings, combine stocks or seasons, or extrapolate beyond the survey domain without a declared model.

desertification_frontiers.unit: hectares and percent of fixed dryland baseline, with land productivity, vegetation cover, soil condition, and carbon-stock components reported separately
desertification_frontiers.geography: named dryland assessment unit, watershed, rangeland, agricultural district, or country reporting boundary
desertification_frontiers.cadence: annual land-condition update with multi-year trend review
desertification_frontiers.transformation: Retain the dryland definition, fixed spatial baseline, land-cover class, productivity trajectory, soil and vegetation observations, climate covariates, management history, degradation criterion, restoration activity, and uncertainty.
desertification_frontiers.uncertainty: Climate variability, sensor changes, land-cover classification, grazing intensity, crop cycles, soil sampling, choice of baseline, and older global assessment methods can change apparent extent and direction.
desertification_frontiers.threshold_provenance: Use the UNCCD reporting framework or a named regional assessment; no single productivity decline or drought year establishes persistent degradation.
desertification_frontiers.failure_behavior: Do not infer persistent degradation from aridity, drought, bare soil, or a one-year vegetation anomaly without a fixed boundary and multi-indicator evidence.

pesticide_spray_drift_zones.unit: active-ingredient mass or concentration by air, deposition, surface, or biological sample with distance, duration, and application context stated
pesticide_spray_drift_zones.geography: named application field, intended treatment boundary, downwind receptor, habitat, or water body
pesticide_spray_drift_zones.cadence: event-based sampling with seasonal incident and compliance review
pesticide_spray_drift_zones.transformation: Retain active ingredient, formulation, application method, nozzle and pressure, droplet class, rate, intended boundary, wind speed and direction, temperature and inversion status, receptor distance, sample matrix, detection limit, label restrictions, and uncertainty.
pesticide_spray_drift_zones.uncertainty: Wind shifts, inversions, volatilization, equipment, droplet size, sampling timing, degradation, background use, and incomplete application records affect exposure estimates.
pesticide_spray_drift_zones.threshold_provenance: Use the product label, EPA risk assessment, and receptor-specific toxicological or ecological benchmark; drift has no universal concentration threshold.
pesticide_spray_drift_zones.failure_behavior: Do not infer exposure from proximity or a complaint alone, combine different active ingredients, or treat lawful application as evidence of off-target movement.

dust_storm_frequency.metric_name: Sand and dust storm event frequency and exposure
dust_storm_frequency.unit: events per season or year, with duration, particulate concentration, aerosol index, visibility, and affected area reported separately
dust_storm_frequency.geography: named source region, transport corridor, monitoring network, or receptor population
dust_storm_frequency.cadence: event observation with seasonal and annual trend review
dust_storm_frequency.transformation: Retain the event definition, source attribution, wind field, soil moisture and cover, land use, aerosol or particulate product, surface stations, plume boundary, transport duration, detection threshold, missing observations, and uncertainty.
dust_storm_frequency.uncertainty: Cloud screening, surface-monitor coverage, event thresholds, source attribution, transported smoke or pollution, soil moisture, and changing satellite products affect counts and exposure estimates.
dust_storm_frequency.threshold_provenance: Use the named WMO warning or monitoring framework and a fixed event definition; aerosol detection alone does not establish a sand or dust storm.
dust_storm_frequency.failure_behavior: Do not combine incomparable event thresholds, infer a land-management cause from a transported plume, or treat missing observations as no event.

atmospheric_river_intensification.metric_name: Atmospheric-river integrated vapor transport intensity and duration
atmospheric_river_intensification.unit: kilograms per metre per second peak integrated vapor transport, hours duration, and event category with detection algorithm stated
atmospheric_river_intensification.geography: named coastal transect, watershed, landfall corridor, or atmospheric-river catalog domain
atmospheric_river_intensification.cadence: six-hourly or finer event detection with seasonal and annual catalog review
atmospheric_river_intensification.transformation: Retain the detection algorithm, integrated-vapor-transport threshold and geometry, reanalysis or forecast product, landfall location, orientation, duration, peak intensity, precipitation, antecedent soil and snow conditions, stream gauges, missing periods, and uncertainty.
atmospheric_river_intensification.uncertainty: Catalogs differ by threshold, geometry, reanalysis, resolution, landfall definition, and duration; topography and antecedent conditions strongly change precipitation and runoff impacts.
atmospheric_river_intensification.threshold_provenance: Use a named atmospheric-river catalog or the published intensity-duration scale; the term intensification requires comparison against a fixed event or climatological baseline.
atmospheric_river_intensification.failure_behavior: Do not compare categories across unmatched algorithms, equate every moisture plume with a landfalling event, or infer flood impact from integrated vapor transport alone.

aviation_condensation_trails.metric_name: Persistent contrail and aviation-induced cloudiness burden
aviation_condensation_trails.unit: kilometres of detected trail, square kilometres or percent cloud fraction, hours persistence, optical depth, and watts per square metre forcing reported separately
aviation_condensation_trails.geography: named flight-information region, air corridor, satellite scene, or model domain
aviation_condensation_trails.cadence: event detection with daily aggregation and seasonal forcing review
aviation_condensation_trails.transformation: Retain aircraft or traffic attribution limits, altitude, engine and fuel context where available, temperature, humidity and ice supersaturation, natural-cirrus screening, detection sensor and algorithm, persistence, spreading, optical properties, day-night state, cloud overlap, forcing method, and uncertainty.
aviation_condensation_trails.uncertainty: Natural cirrus, cloud overlap, ice-supersaturation forecasts, satellite detection, attribution to individual flights, optical properties, day-night balance, and model efficacy dominate uncertainty.
aviation_condensation_trails.threshold_provenance: Use FAA formation criteria and a named satellite or model detection method; a visible line alone does not establish persistence, cloud fraction, or radiative forcing.
aviation_condensation_trails.failure_behavior: Do not infer deliberate dispersal, assign a trail to an individual aircraft without trajectory evidence, or convert occurrence directly into warming without cloud and radiative calculations.

methane_hydroxyl_sink_loss.metric_name: Tropospheric hydroxyl oxidation capacity and methane lifetime
methane_hydroxyl_sink_loss.unit: molecules per cubic centimetre or normalized hydroxyl-radical anomaly, years chemical lifetime, and teragrams per year chemical sink reported separately
methane_hydroxyl_sink_loss.geography: global troposphere or named chemistry-model and observational-inversion domain
methane_hydroxyl_sink_loss.cadence: annual multi-year inversion and chemistry-model assessment
methane_hydroxyl_sink_loss.transformation: Retain hydroxyl definition and weighting, chemical mechanism, methane burden, carbon-monoxide and volatile-organic-compound emissions, nitrogen oxides, water vapour, ozone photolysis, lightning, fire, model ensemble, methyl-chloroform or other observational constraint, averaging period, and uncertainty.
methane_hydroxyl_sink_loss.uncertainty: The radical is too short-lived for a dense direct global network; inversions and models disagree on trends and are sensitive to emissions, transport, chemistry, observational constraints, and spatial weighting.
methane_hydroxyl_sink_loss.threshold_provenance: Use the IPCC methane-lifetime assessment or a named observationally constrained chemistry ensemble; weakening requires a significant decline in oxidation capacity or rise in chemical lifetime against a fixed method.
methane_hydroxyl_sink_loss.failure_behavior: Do not infer a global trend from methane growth alone, combine incompatible lifetime definitions, or attribute changes to one precursor without a full chemistry and emissions sensitivity analysis.

walker_circulation_shift.metric_name: Pacific Walker circulation strength and longitude
walker_circulation_shift.unit: standardized index or pascals sea-level-pressure gradient, metres per second zonal wind, pascals per second vertical velocity, and degrees longitude reported separately
walker_circulation_shift.geography: equatorial Pacific with explicitly stated western and eastern boxes, pressure levels, reanalysis or station network
walker_circulation_shift.cadence: monthly with seasonal ENSO composites and multi-decadal trend review
walker_circulation_shift.transformation: Retain circulation-index definition, pressure and wind boxes, pressure level, reanalysis or station product, sea-surface-temperature gradient, ENSO phase, rainfall field, season, baseline, smoothing, missing data, and uncertainty.
walker_circulation_shift.uncertainty: Different indices, sparse early observations, reanalysis changes, ENSO, volcanic forcing, tropical-basin interactions, and internal decadal variability can change the inferred magnitude or sign of a trend.
walker_circulation_shift.threshold_provenance: Use a named Southern Oscillation, pressure-gradient, trade-wind, mass-streamfunction, or vertical-velocity method; variability is relative to its fixed seasonal baseline and does not imply a monotonic weakening.
walker_circulation_shift.failure_behavior: Do not infer a long-term forced trend from one ENSO event or short reanalysis interval, combine opposite-sign indices without conversion, or treat a pressure anomaly alone as the full overturning circulation.

subsea_cable_landing_chokepoint.metric_name: Submarine-cable landing-site concentration and hazard exposure
subsea_cable_landing_chokepoint.unit: cables, independent systems, landing stations, geographically diverse routes, shared-risk groups, and exposed capacity reported separately
subsea_cable_landing_chokepoint.geography: named country, island, coastline segment, landing station, cable system, or terrestrial backhaul corridor
subsea_cable_landing_chokepoint.cadence: quarterly infrastructure inventory with event-based outage and annual resilience review
subsea_cable_landing_chokepoint.transformation: Retain cable and system identity, ownership independence, landing and station coordinates at an appropriate security resolution, terrestrial backhaul, design capacity, active capacity, route diversity, shared ducts or power, hazard layers, redundancy, rerouting, repair access, outage duration, and uncertainty.
subsea_cable_landing_chokepoint.uncertainty: Public maps omit or generalize routes, ownership and capacity do not equal operational independence, confidential station and backhaul details limit common-mode analysis, and traffic can reroute dynamically.
subsea_cable_landing_chokepoint.threshold_provenance: Use the ITU resilience stress-test framework or a declared network-reliability method; concentration requires an explicit geographic and shared-risk definition rather than a raw cable count.
subsea_cable_landing_chokepoint.failure_behavior: Do not publish sensitive facility detail, equate several cables at one coast with independent redundancy, or infer service loss from physical exposure without topology, traffic, power, backhaul, and restoration evidence.

fishery_border_dispute_zones.metric_name: International fisheries conflict incidents and severity
fishery_border_dispute_zones.unit: events by actor pair, fishery, jurisdiction, incident type, severity, casualties, detention, vessel impact, and duration reported separately
fishery_border_dispute_zones.geography: named transboundary stock, fishing ground, exclusive economic zone, high-seas area, bilateral boundary, or regional fisheries body
fishery_border_dispute_zones.cadence: event-based coding with annual actor-pair and fishery review
fishery_border_dispute_zones.transformation: Retain source documents, actors, flag and coastal states, stock or fishery, location, jurisdiction, incident type, violence or coercion, detention, enforcement, disputed claims, stock status, catch and effort, dependence, governance agreement, climate attribution boundary, coding decision, duplicates, and uncertainty.
fishery_border_dispute_zones.uncertainty: Public reporting is incomplete and politically uneven; incidents may mix fisheries, territorial, security, labour, piracy, or enforcement motives, while stock and dependence data have different spatial and temporal coverage.
fishery_border_dispute_zones.threshold_provenance: Use a documented conflict-event taxonomy and distinguish routine enforcement or diplomatic negotiation from coercive or violent conflict; no raw event count is a universal severity threshold.
fishery_border_dispute_zones.failure_behavior: Do not attribute an incident to climate or scarcity from co-occurrence alone, infer hostility from vessel proximity, double-count syndicated reports, or collapse illegal fishing, enforcement, territorial disputes, and armed conflict into one category.

convective_instability_shift.metric_name: Convective available potential energy and inhibition anomaly
convective_instability_shift.unit: joules per kilogram for parcel-specific CAPE and CIN, with lifted index, humidity, shear, and vertical motion reported separately
convective_instability_shift.geography: named sounding station, satellite pixel, reanalysis grid, forecast domain, or climatological region
convective_instability_shift.cadence: hourly to six-hourly environmental analysis with seasonal and annual climatology review
convective_instability_shift.transformation: Retain parcel definition, virtual-temperature correction, pressure levels, sounding or retrieval source, vertical resolution, surface conditions, moisture, lapse rate, CAPE, CIN, lifted index, shear, forcing or lift, entrainment treatment, baseline, quality flags, and uncertainty.
convective_instability_shift.uncertainty: Values vary sharply with parcel choice, moisture and surface observations; satellite and reanalysis retrievals smooth vertical structure, and unentraining parcel theory overstates realized updraft energy.
convective_instability_shift.threshold_provenance: Use the NOAA product definition or a named sounding method and region-specific climatology; anomaly and severe-weather thresholds must not be transferred across parcel methods or climates.
convective_instability_shift.failure_behavior: Do not infer storm initiation, severity, rainfall, hail, tornadoes, or lightning from CAPE alone; require lift, inhibition, moisture, shear, storm organization, and observed outcomes appropriate to the claim.

lightning_regime_shifts.metric_name: Lightning flash density, extent, and seasonality anomaly
lightning_regime_shifts.unit: flashes per square kilometre per time interval, flash extent area, radiant energy, and season timing reported separately
lightning_regime_shifts.geography: named GLM field of view, LIS or OTD sampling domain, ground-network domain, fixed grid, or climate region
lightning_regime_shifts.cadence: event and five-minute observation with monthly, seasonal, and annual climatology review
lightning_regime_shifts.transformation: Retain sensor and version, event-group-flash clustering, detection efficiency, field of view, view time, day-night state, grid area, total versus cloud-to-ground definition, season, baseline, missing coverage, quality flags, and uncertainty.
lightning_regime_shifts.uncertainty: Satellite and ground networks observe different discharge components; detection efficiency, orbital or viewing geometry, clustering algorithms, network upgrades, day-night background, and short records can create apparent changes.
lightning_regime_shifts.threshold_provenance: Use the NOAA GLM or NASA LIS-OTD product definition and a fixed sensor-specific climatology; anomaly is not interchangeable across sensors without detection-efficiency correction.
lightning_regime_shifts.failure_behavior: Do not interpret optical events as ground strikes, merge uncorrected sensors, infer a climate trend from coverage change, or convert flash density directly into severe-storm or wildfire probability.

cfc_saturated_layers.unit: parts per trillion dry-air mole fraction by species and equivalent effective stratospheric chlorine in parts per trillion chlorine-equivalent reported separately
cfc_saturated_layers.geography: named surface monitoring network and explicitly defined midlatitude or polar stratospheric domain
cfc_saturated_layers.cadence: monthly species observations with annual burden and multi-year trend assessment
cfc_saturated_layers.transformation: Retain gas species, chlorine or bromine content, ozone-depletion weighting, surface abundance, atmospheric lifetime, age-of-air lag, latitude and altitude domain, natural-source treatment, network, calibration scale, scenario, missing data, and uncertainty.
cfc_saturated_layers.uncertainty: Species have different lifetimes, transport lags, photolysis fractions, natural contributions, and per-atom ozone-depletion effectiveness; surface abundance and stratospheric reactive loading are not interchangeable.
cfc_saturated_layers.threshold_provenance: Use the WMO and NOAA assessment definition of equivalent effective stratospheric chlorine for the stated region and year; keep individual CFC, HCFC, halon, methyl-bromide, and other species trends visible.
cfc_saturated_layers.failure_behavior: Do not combine unweighted species, classify HFC replacements as ozone-depleting, infer current stratospheric loading directly from one surface sample, or treat a declining aggregate as evidence that every species is declining.

stratospheric_chlorine_sinks.unit: Dobson Units and million square kilometres below the 220-DU Antarctic threshold
stratospheric_chlorine_sinks.geography: Southern Hemisphere Antarctic ozone-hole domain south of 40 degrees south, with the seasonal averaging window stated
stratospheric_chlorine_sinks.cadence: daily observation with fixed-window annual assessment
stratospheric_chlorine_sinks.transformation: Retain total-column definition, satellite and assimilation systems, polar-vortex domain, 220-DU threshold, fixed seasonal windows, missing years, annual hole area, minimum ozone, quality context and uncertainty separately.
stratospheric_chlorine_sinks.uncertainty: Polar-vortex dynamics, temperature, aerosols, sunlight, transport, sensor transitions, missing-orbit assimilation and the selected seasonal window affect annual ozone-hole area and minimum column ozone.
stratospheric_chlorine_sinks.threshold_provenance: NASA defines the Antarctic ozone hole as the area below 220 Dobson Units because values below that threshold were not observed over Antarctica before 1979 and indicate chlorine- and bromine-related ozone loss.
stratospheric_chlorine_sinks.failure_behavior: Do not conflate stratospheric and ground-level ozone, treat the Antarctic indicator as a spatially uniform global column, fill the missing 1995 year, or attribute a single-season anomaly without chemical and dynamical context.

snowpack_dust_soot_coverage.metric_name: Mineral-dust mass loading and snow albedo
snowpack_dust_soot_coverage.unit: grams per square metre mineral-dust loading, unitless spectral or broadband albedo, and watts per square metre absorbed shortwave energy reported separately
snowpack_dust_soot_coverage.geography: named snow basin, sampling transect, satellite pixel, mountain range, or watershed with source-region context
snowpack_dust_soot_coverage.cadence: event-layer sampling and daily remote sensing during accumulation and melt seasons with annual comparison
snowpack_dust_soot_coverage.transformation: Retain particle mineralogy and size, dust mass, snow depth and water equivalent, layer position, wet or dry deposition, spectral reflectance, grain size, solar geometry, cloud screening, sensor and version, source attribution, melt stage, site, baseline, and uncertainty.
snowpack_dust_soot_coverage.uncertainty: Dust can be buried and re-emerge during melt; snow grain growth, black carbon, algae, forest litter, clouds, slope, aspect, sensor resolution, and mixed pixels also change reflectance and energy absorption.
snowpack_dust_soot_coverage.threshold_provenance: Use the USGS sampling and reflectance method or a named field and remote-sensing protocol; mineral dust must be reported separately from black carbon and biological impurities.
snowpack_dust_soot_coverage.failure_behavior: Do not infer dust mass from visible darkening alone, conflate mineral dust with soot, compare unmatched melt stages or sensors, or transfer a Colorado loading-to-melt relationship without local energy and snowpack modeling.

agrochemical_water_sinks.metric_name: Surface-water pesticide residue concentration and benchmark ratio
agrochemical_water_sinks.unit: micrograms per litre by parent compound or degradate and unitless measured-concentration-to-taxon-specific-benchmark ratio reported separately
agrochemical_water_sinks.geography: named stream, lake, watershed, monitoring station, sampling reach, and upstream use domain
agrochemical_water_sinks.cadence: event and routine water sampling with seasonal and annual mixture review
agrochemical_water_sinks.transformation: Retain active ingredient or degradate, analytical method, reporting limit, censored values, grab or time-integrated sample, dissolved or total fraction, flow, rainfall, upstream application estimate, land use, season, benchmark version and taxon, mixture method, quality controls, and uncertainty.
agrochemical_water_sinks.uncertainty: Short runoff pulses are easily missed; reporting limits, degradates, mixtures, flow, season, treatment practices, urban uses, and changing analytical methods affect occurrence and inferred risk.
agrochemical_water_sinks.threshold_provenance: Compare each measured chemical to the current EPA aquatic-life benchmark or applicable water-quality criterion for the stated taxon and exposure duration; detection alone is not an ecological-effect threshold.
agrochemical_water_sinks.failure_behavior: Do not add unlike compounds into an unweighted total, treat non-detects as zero, infer the source from land use alone, or claim harm solely because a residue was detected.

pesticide_bioaccumulation_chains.metric_name: Persistent pesticide residue in sediment and biota
pesticide_bioaccumulation_chains.unit: micrograms per kilogram dry or wet weight by compound and matrix, with lipid-normalized concentration, biota-sediment accumulation factor, or trophic magnification factor reported separately
pesticide_bioaccumulation_chains.geography: named water body, sediment reach, species, tissue, food-web sample, watershed, and reference site
pesticide_bioaccumulation_chains.cadence: seasonal or annual sediment and tissue sampling with multi-year persistence review
pesticide_bioaccumulation_chains.transformation: Retain parent compound and degradates, sediment grain size and organic carbon, tissue and species, age or size, lipid content, trophic position, wet or dry basis, analytical recovery, reporting limit, water concentration, source history, half-life, hydrophobicity, sampling design, and uncertainty.
pesticide_bioaccumulation_chains.uncertainty: Uptake differs by compound, species, tissue, diet, metabolism, lipid content, trophic position, sediment exposure, season, and legacy contamination; bioaccumulation and biomagnification are not interchangeable.
pesticide_bioaccumulation_chains.threshold_provenance: Use a compound-specific EPA ecological assessment, sediment benchmark, tissue residue guideline, or a documented field-derived accumulation or trophic-magnification method.
pesticide_bioaccumulation_chains.failure_behavior: Do not infer food-web magnification from a single organism, combine compounds or wet- and dry-weight values, equate sediment detection with tissue dose, or assume every pesticide is persistent or bioaccumulative.

biodiversity_corridors_disruption.unit: percent of forest and protected-area network
biodiversity_corridors_disruption.geography: global forest and terrestrial protected-area network
biodiversity_corridors_disruption.transformation: Retain forest-fragment and protected-area structural-connectivity measures separately; join FAO forest-loss history only as persistence context.
biodiversity_corridors_disruption.uncertainty: Structural connectivity is not species-specific functional connectivity; map resolution, patch thresholds and protected-area boundaries affect estimates.
biodiversity_corridors_disruption.threshold_provenance: Use the UNEP-WCMC global structural-connectivity assessment and retain its explicit limitation relative to functional movement.
biodiversity_corridors_disruption.failure_behavior: Do not infer species use, demographic benefit, gene flow or a universal corridor condition from structural connectivity alone.

avian_migration_disruptions.metric_name: Migratory-bird passage timing, route, and stopover use
avian_migration_disruptions.unit: birds or radar bioscatter per kilometre per hour, median passage date, days of phenological offset, stopover occupancy or use probability, and habitat area reported separately
avian_migration_disruptions.geography: named species or guild, radar or observation domain, flyway or route segment, stopover site, breeding and nonbreeding ranges, and annual-cycle boundary
avian_migration_disruptions.cadence: nightly or daily during migration with seasonal summaries and multi-year trend review
avian_migration_disruptions.transformation: Retain species or radar target definition, observation method, effort and detection probability, flight altitude and direction where available, passage date, abundance, stopover arrival and departure, habitat use, food phenology, temperature, precipitation, wind, land cover, route boundary, baseline, missing observations, and uncertainty.
avian_migration_disruptions.uncertainty: Weather radar cannot always identify species, citizen-science effort changes, routes and cues differ among populations, stopover use varies with weather and habitat, and an earlier date does not by itself indicate harm.
avian_migration_disruptions.threshold_provenance: Use a named species, observation network, migration season, route or stopover boundary, and fixed phenological baseline; disruption requires a significant change in timing, route use, habitat access, or resource overlap rather than movement itself.
avian_migration_disruptions.failure_behavior: Do not combine species with different strategies into one trend, equate flyway geography with an observed route, infer demographic harm from timing change alone, or attribute a single-season anomaly to climate or habitat loss.

high_altitude_forest_shrinkage.unit: hectares and percent cover change, metres elevation or kilometres latitude of boundary movement, and tree density or basal area reported separately
high_altitude_forest_shrinkage.geography: named mountain range, elevation band, forest type, species assemblage, ecotone, fixed land-cover grid, and disturbance perimeter
high_altitude_forest_shrinkage.cadence: annual remote-sensing update with five-year inventory and multi-decadal boundary review
high_altitude_forest_shrinkage.transformation: Retain forest and treeline definitions, species, elevation, slope and aspect, sensor and version, canopy threshold, plot inventory, snowpack, soil moisture, temperature, drought, fire and insect history, regeneration, land use, baseline, persistence rule, attribution method, and uncertainty.
high_altitude_forest_shrinkage.uncertainty: Upper boundaries may expand while dry lower margins contract; fire, insects, harvest, classification change, delayed regeneration, and transient canopy loss can mimic a persistent climate-driven range change.
high_altitude_forest_shrinkage.threshold_provenance: Require a named ecological boundary and persistent cover, density, regeneration, or treeline displacement against a fixed baseline; report upper expansion and lower contraction separately.
high_altitude_forest_shrinkage.failure_behavior: Do not interpret one fire scar as range contraction, infer net mountain-forest loss from treeline movement alone, combine different canopy definitions, or assume warming has the same sign at cold- and moisture-limited boundaries.

amphibian_chytrid_fungus_spreads.metric_name: Amphibian chytrid infection prevalence, intensity, and mortality
amphibian_chytrid_fungus_spreads.unit: percent polymerase-chain-reaction-positive individuals, genomic equivalents per skin swab, diagnosed deaths, apparent survival, and occupied breeding sites reported separately
amphibian_chytrid_fungus_spreads.geography: named pathogen species, amphibian host taxon and life stage, wetland or stream site, population, sampling region, and surveillance boundary
amphibian_chytrid_fungus_spreads.cadence: seasonal host and environmental sampling with event-based mortality investigation and annual occupancy review
amphibian_chytrid_fungus_spreads.transformation: Retain Bd or Bsal identity, host species and life stage, swab and PCR protocol, genomic load, diagnostic pathology, live or dead status, effort, detection probability, temperature, moisture and water contact, season, site occupancy, prior exposure, co-infection, population trend, baseline, quality controls, and uncertainty.
amphibian_chytrid_fungus_spreads.uncertainty: Detection varies with swabbing, season, temperature, host species, life stage, infection load, prior exposure, and imperfect detection; infection can be widespread and subclinical without attributable mortality.
amphibian_chytrid_fungus_spreads.threshold_provenance: Use pathogen- and host-specific diagnostic standards and a declared infection-load, pathology, survival, or occupancy method; positive detection, clinical disease, mortality, and population decline are separate outcomes.
amphibian_chytrid_fungus_spreads.failure_behavior: Do not infer death or decline from a positive swab, combine Bd and Bsal, compare unmatched PCR protocols, attribute undiagnosed mortality to one pathogen, or treat a temperature association as a universal causal trend.

aerosolized_microplastics.metric_name: Airborne microplastic concentration and deposition flux
aerosolized_microplastics.unit: polymer-confirmed particles per cubic metre of air and particles per square metre per day of wet or dry deposition reported separately, stratified by size, morphology, and polymer
aerosolized_microplastics.geography: named indoor or outdoor sampling site, airshed, deposition station, source facility, trajectory domain, and land or water receptor
aerosolized_microplastics.cadence: event or daily air sampling and weekly deposition collection with seasonal method-matched review
aerosolized_microplastics.transformation: Retain sampler and inlet, sampled air volume or collector area, wet or dry deposition mode, size cutoffs, filter composition, blank correction, contamination controls, microscopy screen, polymer-confirmation method, morphology, colour, mass where validated, meteorology, trajectory, source setting, reporting limit, recovery, and uncertainty.
aerosolized_microplastics.uncertainty: Fibres and fragments occur in heterogeneous particle mixtures; contamination, visual misidentification, sampler design, lower size limit, polymer-confirmation coverage, recovery, and the lack of standardized methods can dominate comparisons.
aerosolized_microplastics.threshold_provenance: Use a declared chemically confirmed particle method and matrix-specific blank correction; air concentration, wet deposition, dry deposition, particle count, and mass are non-interchangeable metrics.
aerosolized_microplastics.failure_behavior: Do not classify visual fibres as plastic without chemical confirmation, compare unmatched size cutoffs or samplers, convert counts to mass without particle-specific evidence, infer health harm from detection alone, or interpret one deposition sample as a global trend.

gulf_stream_slowdown.metric_name: Gulf Stream section transport and path position
gulf_stream_slowdown.unit: Sverdrups of volume transport, kilometres or degrees latitude of a declared path contour, metres per second of velocity, and centimetres of cross-current dynamic sea-level difference reported separately
gulf_stream_slowdown.geography: named current segment and cross-stream section such as the Florida Straits at 27 degrees north, Cape Hatteras separation region, or downstream longitude band with depth and contour definitions
gulf_stream_slowdown.cadence: daily transport and altimetry observation with monthly, annual, and multi-decadal method-consistent assessment
gulf_stream_slowdown.transformation: Retain section coordinates, depth range, cable calibration or ship, pressure-gauge, altimetry or glider method, geomagnetic and tidal corrections, sea-surface-height contour, transport component, uncertainty, gaps, platform version, reference period, and whether the quantity represents the Florida Current, downstream path, total upper flow, or overturning contribution.
gulf_stream_slowdown.uncertainty: Transport increases downstream through entrainment, path and volume transport are different, vertical layers can vary incoherently, cable and satellite records require corrections, and wind-driven gyre flow is not interchangeable with overturning.
gulf_stream_slowdown.threshold_provenance: Use a named NOAA section or peer-reviewed path index with a fixed depth, contour, method, and baseline; slowdown means a statistically supported decline in that exact quantity, not a generic basin-wide claim.
